title: How to disseminate your research?
en:
*Links to concurrent work*

Provide readers a complete landscape of concurrent work. 

"Credits are not like money. Giving credit to others does not diminish the credit you get from your paper." - Simon Peyton Jones

Examples:
• https://phog.github.io/snerg/
• https://alexyu.net/plenoctrees/

title: How to disseminate your research?
en:
*Easy installation*

The easier the installation of your work/code for others, the wider adoption it will be. 

Examples:
• pip install (@rzhang88)
• PyTorch hub

en: @Samujjwal_Sam ABSOLUTELY! Think about all the countless hours on literature survey, research discussions, implementation, experiments, and writing. I would say the time spent on dissemination is the most cost-effective thing you can do to maximize your impact.

title: How to disseminate your research?
en:
@LChoshen I am not an expert so take my words with a grain of salt. 

The very first few seconds are important to get people's attention. Show your BEST results instead of a boring title/author/affiliation page (unless you are famous). Keep only the essence of your work.
How to ask research questions?

title: How to ask research questions?
en:
How to ask research questions?

Zoom fatigue is real 😱. How do you provide feedback to students when you have zero idea about what their work is about (because you have been scrolling the twitter feed)? Here are some boilerplate questions that you can use. 🧵

title: How to ask research questions?
en:
*Why should I (or someone else) care?*

What will the field change with your work? This helps remind students of finding their core motivation of the work.

title: How to ask research questions?
en:
*When will you use it?*

Contextualizing your research work with practical applications helps identify potentially unrealistic constraints/assumptions.

title: How to ask research questions?
en:
*What other people have done and why they are not satisfactory?*

If existing methods work well already, why do you need to work on this research project?

title: How to ask research questions?
en:
*Which is the closest related work and how does yours differ?*

Articulate the core novelty of your work.

title: How to ask research questions?
en:
*How did you know it is working (better than prior work)?*

Are all the claims validated? Are the experiments fair? Are the results representative for the application domains?

title: How to ask research questions?
en:
*What would you do if you have another 3 months?*

Think about how to maximally strengthen the work with a specific time budget.

How to improve asynchronous communication?

title: How to improve asynchronous communication?
en:
How to improve asynchronous communication? 

Two years into remote work, asynchronous communication has never been this important for work efficiency and productivity. 

Some tips for effective async communication 🧵

title: How to improve asynchronous communication?
en:
*One topic at a time*

❌ Here are the results of the experiments we discussed. BTW, can you approve my conference travel expense?

✅ Conference travel expense - Approval required by April 20.

title: How to improve asynchronous communication?
en:
*Formatting*

❌ Writing loooong free-form paragraphs.

✅ Writing structured, concise, clear texts. Formatting tools (bold, underscore, italic, itemize, enumerate, paragraph, line breaks) are your friends.

title: How to improve asynchronous communication?
en:
*Inline content*

❌ I made an overview figure here <JPEG link> and wrote down the math derivation here <PDF link>.

✅ Embed the content inline.

title: How to improve asynchronous communication?
en:
*Async sharing before sync meeting*

❌ Describe your work, show results during the meeting.

✅ Summarize your work/results and send them for early feedback before the meeting. Make the best use of your favorite collaborative document platforms.

title: How to improve asynchronous communication?
en:
*Actionable next steps after a sync meeting*

❌ Just talked. Brainstormed multiple ideas. Created a bunch of tasks.

✅ Decide WHO to do WHAT by WHEN.

title: How to improve asynchronous communication?
en:
*Give others control when setting up meetings*

❌ When will you be available next week? 

✅ I am available in the following time slots. When will work best for you? Use calendar tools (calendly, google calendar) to avoid back and forth discussions.

title: How to improve asynchronous communication?
en:
*Agenda, agenda, agenda*

❌ Let's hop on a call and chat next week.

✅ Send clear meeting agenda with allocated time.
How to communicate clearly?

title: How to communicate clearly?
en:
How to communicate clearly?

Majority of our time goes into emails, slack messages, and loads of meetings. 

Yet, as a student, no one taught me how to communicate well. (I must have annoyed a lot of people along the way ...😬)

Here is a template for organizing your message.

title: How to communicate clearly?
en:
*(1) What?*

What's your key point? Please don't tell a convoluted story that graaaadually leads to your main point. Ain't nobody got time for that!

👉 Identify your main message and put them up front.

title: How to communicate clearly?
en:
*(2) So What?*

Why is it relevant or important for your work/project/team? Why should your audience care? 🤷‍♂️🤷‍♀️

👉 Tell me why?

title: How to communicate clearly?
en:
*(3) Now What?*

What are the *actionable* steps next? 
e.g., Set up another meeting? Ask for feedback? Outline a plan for a new task?

👉 Call for specific action!

title: How to communicate clearly?
en:
Example: Research

1⃣ What? 
Here are the results of a toy problem A.

2⃣ So what?
This is important because the experiment helps us  study only problem A and not get distracted by problem B/C.

3⃣ Now what?
I will move on to study problem B and C.

title: How to communicate clearly?
en:
Example: Opportunity

1⃣ What? 
I am interested in working with you.

2⃣ So what?
I have relevant skills, experiences, and specific ideas on how to extend your recent work X to Y and Z.

3⃣ Now what?
When would you be available so I can present these specific directions?

title: How to communicate clearly?
en:
Happy communicating!

Having the What/So What/Now What template in mind when writing and speaking about ANYTHING has been very helpful for keeping my messages clear and concise!

Hope this helps yours too! 👍
How to set up a good calendar invite?

title: How to set up a good calendar invite?
en:
How to Set Up a Good Calendar Invite?

Our days are filled with events on the calendar (e.g., project meetings, roundtable, committee, 1:1s) 🗓️ 

But, most calendar invites are awfully vague and lead to unproductive meetings. 

Five tips on writing a good calendar invite 👇

title: How to set up a good calendar invite?
en:
*1⃣ Specific Title*

Nobody knows what "project update" or "internship meeting weekly" are. 🙄

Labeling your event with a specific title helps everyone!

title: How to set up a good calendar invite?
en:
*2⃣ Goal*

Write down specific goals of the meeting! 

You are asking people's time. In the calendar invite, tell them what do you want to achieve from the meeting. 

Make sure to review the goal near the end of each meeting.

title: How to set up a good calendar invite?
en:
*3⃣ Agenda*

Have multiple topics to discuss? 

Write them down and allocate specific time required for each topic.

Don't attend a meeting without an agenda.

title: How to set up a good calendar invite?
en:
*4⃣ Meeting Pre-work*

List the tasks you want your attendee to complete PRIOR to the meeting. 

When everyone is ready, the meeting will be a lot more effective.

title: How to set up a good calendar invite?
en:
*5⃣ Easy-to-Access Information*

❌ zoom meeting ID     
✅ zoom meeting link

❌ "I just sent my slides in the chat."
✅ include link (doc/slides) in the calendar invite

Everything the attendee need should be one click away in the calendar invite.
How to get remembered?

title: How to get remembered?
en:
How to get remembered?

With tens of thousands of papers published each year, how can you ensure that your talk, work, or paper will be remembered? 🤔

Check out Winston’s star 💫!

title: How to get remembered?
en:
*Symbol*

Include a visual symbol that manifests the core of your work. 

Polish that single logo 🦇, picture 🖼️, drawing ✏️, graph 📈, or figure 🏞️!

title: How to get remembered?
en:
*Slogan*

Include a short, slogan-like phrase to serve as a handle for your work. 

Your slogan should 
• evoke the key concept,
• capture the uniqueness of your work, and 
• be memorable.

title: How to get remembered?
en:
*Salient*

Your work usually has several different ideas. Pick the idea that sticks out, not just an important idea.

Squeezing many ideas in one talk is a bad idea.

title: How to get remembered?
en:
*Surprise*

Highlight a surprise in your work. We all love surprises!

title: How to get remembered?
en:
*Story*

Humans are drawn to stories. Stories let us create an emotional connection and resonate with their own experience. 

Describe how you did it, with whom, when, and where?

title: How to get remembered?
en:
Want to make your work memorable? Include

🌟 Symbol
🌟 Slogan
🌟 Salient
🌟 Surprise
🌟 Story

and don't forget to watch the talk "How to Speak" by Prof. Patrick Winston! It's beyond amazing!  
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Unzc731iCUY
How to schedule a meeting?

title: How to schedule a meeting?
en:
How to schedule a meeting?

When you ask for a meeting with others, you are asking for their time. You are asking for their most valuable, finite resource to benefit yourself (e.g., for advice, networking, questions, and opportunities). 

Here are some tips that I found useful.

title: How to schedule a meeting?
en:
*Provide your availability upfront*

The most annoying thing you can do is to ask:

"Can you give me a list of time slots when you are available?"

This basically asks people to put ALL their availability ON HOLD for a meeting with you.
